name: Quijorna
story: Quijorna was one of the Nationalist strongpoints that blunted the Republic's Brunete offensive. Its small garrison held out for three days against Republican divisions before falling on 9 July 1937, costing the attackers time they could not afford. The surrounding hills were then fortified by both sides. Around the village survive a hilltop bunker and, some 2 km behind the Republican line of Cota 640 and Loma Quemada, the camp of La Peña, while the farmhouse of Casa de los Llanos served as a Republican planning centre.
see: A concrete bunker on the hill above the village and remains of the Republican rear camp at La Peña.
plan: Free; walk up from the village. Combine with Brunete and Villanueva de la Cañada.
